verdict.rationale: Sentry's own docs say you can run all of Sentry on your own server for free. Hands-on reports confirm long-running self-hosted deployments that are rock-solid once running, and users value self-hosting as an escape hatch from the SaaS. The caveats are real but secondary: the self-hosted version comes with no guarantees or dedicated support, it is described as for simple use cases, users report heavy resource growth (one 32GB server ran nothing but Sentry), and self-hosted releases lag behind SaaS launches. Missing for 10: official support or guarantees for self-hosted deployments, documented production-scale sizing guidance, feature parity and release timing with SaaS.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
Sentry offers and maintains a minimal setup that works out-of-the-box for simple use cases.
They have run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and it has worked fantastically; once running it is rock-solid.
